t: You're facing Kensington Central Library, a Grade II* listed building on Hornton Street and Phillimore Walk, right next to Kensington Town Hall. It was built between 1958 and 1960 to a design by E. Vincent Harris, an architect who designed several important public buildings in traditional styles. That's why it is in an English Renaissance style. Some people demonstrated against the plan because they wanted a modern building. It replaced a Gothic house called The Abbey, which was destroyed by bombing in 1944. The Queen Mother opened the library on 13 July 1960.
